function_map.note: v3: proven extents (masked/accepted rows) end where the next function starts, and no start may lie inside a proven extent. Adds 0x9480, removes the jump-table span 0x1ab30. A RET-on-boundary + prologue heuristic was tried and rejected: 9 of its 10 extra starts were inside functions whose extents workers had established.

language_findings: VC5 C++ front end uses the loaded global pointer as SIB base and as add destination; the C front end never does (9-form minimal sweep).
0x8a50, 0x8ed0, 0x92e0, 0x18a90 masked equal only as C++ with typed record indexing; 0x65e0 only as C (constant strcpy lowering); 0x66f0 needs C++ (10 bytes left vs 104 as C).
All installed VC5 revisions (RTM, SP2, NT5 SDK 1592/1691, SP3) give identical results on the near-miss set.

B5.summary: candidate: record-loop anchor register (VC5 anchors strength-reduced loops at the first accessed field).
B5.update_2026_10_09: 0x8770 (C++): a pointer bumped before the load (`p++; x = *p;`) anchors the walking pointer at the base with [p+4] as in the original; `x = p[1]; p++;` folds the +4 into the start address.

B6.observation: VC5 does enregister 0/1 constants in callee-saved registers across calls for ordinary source: 43 masked-equal TITLE functions show it (smallest 0x4b00, 80 bytes: 1 in ebx, 0 in esi). The residue is register-assignment priority, not enregistration itself.
B6.representative: 0x10670 (896 bytes, 35 differing): original buttons->esi and out->ebp; ours the reverse, with identical use counts per register in both binaries (26 vs 19).

B6.reentry: A source form for 0x10670 or a sibling in which buttons carries more live references than are visible as separate code (references merged by the compiler), or in which out references fall in discounted positions; test such a form on a second sibling before generalizing.

allocation_probe.method: Synthetic and cut-down variants of the 0x10670 lead compiled with pinned VC5 RTM /O2; roles read from the listing (about 45 probes, bounded). Scratch: candidates/b6-alloc (ignored).
allocation_probe.prediction: Register priority among callee-saved candidates follows reference weight; a cut-down pair of the same shape with different roles isolates the weight rule.
allocation_probe.falsifier: No single-feature change flips the roles of the buttons local and the out parameter.
allocation_probe.positive_control_pair: Cut-down 0x10670 with only inner cases 1 and 3 as a flat switch: buttons->esi, out->edi. Adding one more live reference to out anywhere (entry block, a case, inside an if) flips to out->esi, buttons->edi; adding three live references to buttons moves it to the top.
findings: Priority follows source-level live reference counts: two variants with identical machine-level register occurrence counts (tails merged by the compiler) differ in roles, so weights are counted before tail merging.
References in unreachable code (if (0)) and self-assignments do not count.
References inside if statements are not discounted; one reference in a switch default case did not flip where one elsewhere did, two did: default references weigh less.
Translation-unit context does not affect roles: renaming the variables, 40 preceding functions, 300 preceding externs or 200 preceding string initializers left 0x10670 unchanged.
Equivalent spellings of the buttons definition (mask, extra statement, separate unsigned short local) either keep buttons last or change its load instruction.

allocation_probe.verdict: Rule partly characterized (count-based, pre-merge, default discounted). Under it the original 0x10670 needs buttons to outweigh both out (about 20 references) and the constant 1, which its two visible tests cannot do; the source must hold live buttons references that the binary does not show as separate code, or out references the compiler discounts. Not resolved; stopped at the bound.

B6.resolved_2026_10_09: Resolved for the screen-handler family (0x10670, 0x102f0, 0x109f0, 0x16f0, 0x13ba0) by the tail-placement lever; see register_study.

B7.observation: Not an xor-vs-mov zero: the original keeps a byte index from 0 with the array address as displacement; VC5 emits a pointer walk in all 13 ordinary loop forms tried, in C and C++, with and without the preceding fill loop.
B7.reentry: Evidence that the index is live or shared beyond the loop in the original, or another function showing the same shape.

context_experiment.hypothesis: Residual differences of near-misses come from compiling them standalone instead of after their matched neighbours.
context_experiment.method: Each near-miss inserted in address order into its region/unit file with reconciled declarations, plus a declarations-only control; all original region functions re-checked.
context_experiment.conclusion: In-context, declarations-only and standalone differences are identical for all seven; every region function stayed masked equal. File context does not explain these residues (unlike ENG1 0x2a520).

context_count_scan.origin: Adopted from blood2_recon docs/object_residue.md: VC5 C++ codegen (register choice, operand order, scheduling) depends on the translation-unit symbol count, often periodically or with thresholds.
context_count_scan.tool: scripts/count_scan.py (diagnostic; prepends N dummy declarations to a scratch copy; never staged or promoted)
context_count_scan.prediction: Some TITLE near-misses are TU-context residue reproduced by a count shift.
context_count_scan.falsifier: No near-miss changes over N = 0..255 (0..1023 for 0x10670).

results.c_front_end: Insensitive. 0x10670 (N 0..1023), 0x1de0 (extern, global, typedef, prototype and struct-tag padding, N 0..159), 0x4aa0, 0x5fb0, 0x13ba0, 0x1a180 (N 0..255): residue constant at every N. CORRECTION 2026-10-09: not universal. Staged C row 0x17bf0 is count-sensitive (windows of N with 51 differing bytes, prototypes counting 2); adding one header to r16110 broke it, so that file keeps its declaration count (a local extern for g_engine_paths).
results.cpp_front_end: 0x8770 is count-sensitive with thresholds: 43 bytes for N < 48, 41 for 48-56, 39 for 57-59, 37 for N >= 60. Each step is one [base+index] operand-order flip. Prototype padding halves the thresholds (24/29/30), so a prototype counts as 2, as blood2 measured. 0x66f0 changes size above N = 69. 0x2090, 0x2860, 0x3050 are insensitive in 0..255.
results.staged_cpp_rows: All 19 masked-equal C++ rows (u08140.cpp, r189e0.cpp) stay masked equal for every N in 0..255.
results.0x8770_follow_up: At N >= 60 the remaining residue is the B5 loop anchor plus an esi/edi swap. The spelling `p++; reca = *p;` reproduces the original anchor ([edi+4], add edi,4), leaving 21 bytes: the counter and the pointer swap esi and edi. That swap does not respond to count, kind, declaration order, or reuse of the earlier loop counter.

context_count_scan.verdict: Partly confirmed. In C++ units, base/index order (B1-like) is TU-count context, so C++ near-misses must be judged at realistic counts. The real headers decide that count; padding is never a fix. The tested C near-misses (B1 in 0x1de0, B6 in 0x10670, B2, 0x4aa0, 0x13ba0, 0x1a180) are count-insensitive, so they are source-form questions; but C code can be count-sensitive (0x17bf0), so header changes need a full masked verify.

register_study.R1: Callee-saved candidates ranked by weight take esi, edi, ebx, ebp in that order (five pointer parameters with descending counts; reversing the counts reverses the mapping); a fifth candidate is not enregistered.
register_study.R2: Ties go to the first source reference (straight-line code); inside loops not established.
register_study.R3: Constants weigh less: a store-source constant outranks a base pointer only when its uses exceed twice the pointer's; constants used only as call arguments are not enregistered; variables need 2 references, store constants 4.
register_study.R5: A ranked constant can hold a register slot while being emitted as immediates, leaving the slot unused; this explains 0x13ba0's push ebx/ebp/esi with self in ebx.
register_study.R6: Plain reference counts do not fully explain weights (adding references to self lowered its rank); some normalisation is involved, not established.
register_study.results: 0x13ba0 masked equal with case 1 writing its own tail and return (as seq1 does); 0x3050 masked equal with v1 = v2 = expr (one fewer v1 reference). 0x9a40/0xa020 are scratch-register rotations (eax->edx->ecx carried across cases, mod 3 temporaries), not callee-saved; re-entry: find the source form in cases 7/2 that changes the temporary count by one.
register_study.R6_refined: Weights are counted before tail merging and a reference in a common tail weighs more than the same reference repeated inside switch cases (0x10670: four out stores in the common tail move out from 4th to 2nd rank; seven are needed inside one case). Constant weights depend on the pointer they are stored through. Leaf functions also rank scratch registers (eax, ecx, edx, esi, edi, ebx); references folded into a shared address temporary do not count for the index variable (0xcd30). Main lever for screen-handler parameter roles: per-case tails versus one common tail. 0x102f0 gets the original roles with the common-tail form (604 -> 365 bytes; structural residue remains). 0x18b20 (14) is scratch allocation/scheduling, not callee-saved; 0x3100 (648) still ranks stream below cell and gives flags no callee-saved register.
register_study.screen_handlers: 0x102f0, 0x109f0, 0x16f0 masked equal with one form: the inner cases break to a tail written inside case 1, while 0xffff breaks to the outer tail. The two uses of the constant 1 then have separate live ranges, so each path loads its register where the original does. All-common-tail and all-own-tail forms each miss (365/439/578 vs 277 bytes). The B6 blocker for this family is resolved.
